headline: Correction: the 1.16 in HRRR downpour hour around 1 AM Wednesday looks like a glitch in the data feed, not a real forecast; every model, HRRR included, otherwise has only light rain Tuesday night, far below street-flooding amounts.

summary.text: Correction to the 7:20 AM discussion: HRRR's 1.16 in hour at 1 AM Wednesday appears to be a data-feed error. HRRR on Windy shows no such burst. Without it, HRRR is light rain.
Excluding the bad hour, HRRR is light: 0.02 to 0.16 in per hour. RRFS 0.08, NBM 0.04, ECMWF 0.01 in for their wettest 3 hours. GFS repeats HRRR's bad hour.
No street flooding expected. The rating card's consensus is 0.08 in; Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour.
Dry today and Tuesday daytime. Light rain about 7 PM Tuesday to early Wednesday morning, wettest late Tuesday evening. Thanksgiving dry; weekend rain possible.
Evening rain falls near the -1.5 ft low at 6:28 PM Tuesday, so the channel can drain. Tides run about 1.4 ft above prediction at highs. Channel low: 0.13 ft.
Clear street drain grates and yard drains today, as NWS advises. Tuesday's gusts may cause outages. The HRRR-only chart may still show the false spike; ignore it.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: The calm before the storm: dry today and tonight as a ridge builds east, with high clouds streaming in. NWS San Francisco (7:06 AM update) calls today the day to clear storm drains and gutters ahead of a moderate rain and wind storm Tuesday afternoon into Wednesday morning, as a shortwave trough and cold front cross Northern California. NWS rain totals are unchanged since its 1:25 AM forecast: 0.4 to 1.0 in for the San Francisco Peninsula and 0.15 to 0.5 in for the East and South Bays, with wiggle room either way depending on the low's track. Winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 40 mph near the coast and through gaps. A general thunder risk (heavy downpours possible with any storm that forms), best north of the Golden Gate. Dry Thanksgiving and Friday; wet weather favored for the weekend. The Coastal Flood Warning for the Bay shoreline is now in effect.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Correction, 8 AM: the 7:20 AM discussion treated a single 1.16 in HRRR hour around 1 AM Wednesday as a possible downpour. It is almost certainly an error in the Open-Meteo HRRR feed the dashboard uses: it sits between two 0.02 in hours, no independent model has anything like it, the GFS series repeats the identical value because it borrows HRRR there, it was unchanged in a second snapshot at 7:53 AM, and HRRR as displayed on Windy shows no such burst. Please disregard it, including on the dashboard's HRRR-only view, until the feed moves past that run.

Wettest 3 hours / storm total, 7 AM Monday to 7 AM Thursday:
• HRRR (extended run, ends 4 AM Wednesday): light rain 10 PM Tuesday onward at 0.02 to 0.04 in per hour, then 0.13 and 0.16 in hours around 3 and 4 AM Wednesday. With the bad hour included, the feed gives 1.30 / 1.55 in, and that is what the consensus math sees.
• RRFS (10 PM Sun run): 0.08 / 0.16 in, wettest 8 to 11 PM Tuesday, one 0.06 in hour around 7 AM Wednesday. Unchanged.
• NBM: 0.04 / 0.12 in, down from 0.11 / 0.42 in. Only 0.01 in per hour, 7 to 11 PM Tuesday.
• ECMWF: 0.01 / 0.04 in, down from 0.08 / 0.13 in. Almost dry.
• GFS: matches HRRR hour for hour 10 PM Tuesday to 1 AM Wednesday, including the bad value, so it adds no information.

Consensus (HRRR × 1.25, RRFS 0.08, NBM 0.04): middle value 0.08 in, down from 0.11 in, so the rating card stays at none. Because the consensus takes the middle value, the bad HRRR hour does not move it. The usual caveats stand: HRRR-type guidance has under-forecast local bursts here by about 3×, NWS keeps a general thunder risk with the front, and NWS's Peninsula range (0.4 to 1.0 in) is above every independent model's total for the street.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model runs about 1.4 ft above the predicted high tides at Redwood City (1.0 to 1.7 ft at the lows). This morning's 9.2 ft high at 10:20 AM runs about 10.6 ft; tonight's 7.0 ft high at 12:16 AM Tuesday about 8.4 ft; Tuesday's 9.5 ft high at 11:02 AM about 10.9 ft. Tuesday evening's light rain falls near the predicted -1.5 ft low at 6:28 PM, with the model near -0.3 ft at 7 PM and 3.6 ft at 10 PM, so the channel can drain. The model has the water at 7.2 ft at midnight and 8.3 ft at 1 AM Wednesday (its last hour), near the predicted 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM, so any rain still falling then would drain more slowly. Wednesday's 9.5 ft king tide at 11:46 AM comes after all models have the rain over.

NWS: Coastal Flood Warning for the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines, 6:10 AM Monday to 4 PM Thursday, with up to 2.7 ft of inundation possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. San Francisco high tides 2.0 ft above normal today, 2.4 ft Tuesday, 2.7 ft Wednesday and 2.2 ft Thursday, including up to 1.5 ft of surge, approaching the highest tide ever recorded there.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas it reads 0.13 ft at 7 AM, flat between 0.12 and 0.17 ft for 24 hours (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at 5:13 AM (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry and calm on the street this morning. The Caltrain rain gauge recorded no rain in the 24 hours to 5:13 AM. NWS reports dense Tule fog in the interior valleys and high clouds moving in; the Bay shoreline is seeing significant coastal flooding at this morning's high tide.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low through Tuesday afternoon: dry. Moderate for Tuesday evening into Wednesday morning: all models bring only light rain, wettest 0.01 to 0.08 in per 3 hours among the independent ones. The open questions are whether NWS's higher Peninsula totals or the drier point models verify, and whether a thunderstorm cell on the front gives a short downpour no model shows. The false HRRR hour should drop out once the next extended HRRR run reaches the dashboard.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Today and Tuesday morning: clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains, and check sandbags.
• Tuesday afternoon and evening: gusts to 40 mph possible; outages can slow the pumps.
• Tuesday evening: keep this page open in case a downpour develops; timestamped photos at the peak help.
• Stay away from the Bay shore and tidal sloughs at the late-morning high tides through Thursday; don't walk or drive through moving water.
